task.description:
Design the fix for ISS-0630 / GH #605 (BLOCKER): 9 migration files declare
'-- scope: public' but perform unqualified CREATE TABLE / INSERT INTO work,
which trips the declaresUnqualifiedTableWork() scope-mismatch guard
(src/db/migrations.zig) on any genuinely fresh database. This breaks fresh-
database migration bootstrap on main. The defect was introduced by commit
a2a8c68 (ISS-0185 / GH#518, merged 2026-08-08), which added the scope headers
without qualifying the table statements with public. It is invisible on every
long-lived shared db_test container because those files' ledger rows were
already recorded applied before the defect entered their content.

Affected files and their unqualified statements (confirmed by direct inspection):
- migrations/011_webhook_subscriptions.sql: CREATE TABLE metric_snapshots, CREATE TABLE rate_limit_buckets
- migrations/022_obs06_alerting_state.sql: CREATE TABLE obs_alert_trigger_state, CREATE TABLE obs_alert_hook_emission_state
- migrations/038_oidc_claim_mapping_config.sql: CREATE TABLE realm_claim_mapping_config
- migrations/039_jit_provisioning_config.sql: CREATE TABLE jit_provisioning_config, INSERT INTO jit_provisioning_config
- migrations/041_oidc15_realm_deletion_tracker.sql: CREATE TABLE realm_deletion_tracker
- migrations/042_oidc16_26_agent_lifecycle_foundations.sql: CREATE TABLE idp_operation_ledger, idp_transaction_log, idp_adapter_audit
- migrations/049_repository_service_catalog.sql: CREATE TABLE service_catalog
- migrations/056_onboarding_registry.sql: CREATE TABLE onboarding_registry
- migrations/094_entity_subsystem.sql: INSERT INTO event_type_registry

All nine tables are genuinely global/platform-wide (metrics, rate limiting,
OIDC realm config, onboarding registry, service catalog, alerting state, entity
event-type registry) -- none are per-tenant business data. The fix should
therefore qualify each unqualified CREATE TABLE / ALTER TABLE / INSERT INTO
statement with the public. schema prefix, NOT change the scope header to
'-- scope: all_schemas' (that would incorrectly cause the migration runner to
apply per-tenant work that these tables do not need).

IMPORTANT: these 9 files have ALREADY been applied (ledger-recorded) on every
existing long-lived db_test/dev database, with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS making
them idempotent no-ops on those databases going forward -- so this is a pure
content-correctness fix for future fresh-database bootstraps, not a data migration
or backfill. Do not write a corrective/backfill migration; edit the 9 files in place.

Design should also state whether any test/CI gate should be added or updated to
catch this defect class on a fresh database going forward (this is the second
occurrence -- see ISS-0603/GH-467 and ISS-0604/GH-470, the latter of which built
the very guard that caught this one) -- note in the design if such a gate already
exists and simply was not run against a fresh database, versus needing to be built.

This is a small, well-bounded, single-root-cause fix. Do not expand scope to the
35 residual test-integration-svc failures noted in the diagnosis -- those remain
explicitly out of scope for this run, blocked on this fix landing first, and will
be addressed in a later run once a trustworthy fresh-database measurement is possible.
acceptance_criteria: Design covers all 9 affected migration files
Design specifies public.-qualification (not scope-header change) for each unqualified statement, consistent with these tables being genuinely global
Design explicitly excludes the 35 residual test-integration-svc failures from this fix scope
Design notes whether a fresh-database CI/test gate already exists or needs to be added to prevent recurrence
No design element requires a backfill or corrective data migration -- these are idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / already-applied-elsewhere statements

result.summary: Designed the ISS-0630/GH-605 fix: qualify unqualified CREATE TABLE/INSERT INTO statements with public. in all 9 migration files, confirmed via direct read of declaresUnqualifiedTableWork() in src/db/migrations.zig that the guard checks CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE/DROP TABLE/INSERT INTO heads only (not CREATE INDEX), scans the ENTIRE file body (not a truncated header), and is unaffected by DO 122119 block boundaries -- so all 4 unqualified statements in 094_entity_subsystem.sql (including the INSERT INTO event_type_registry ~80 lines after the scope comment) require qualification. Confirmed zero REFERENCES/FK clauses across all 9 files (no intra-file cross-references needing qualification beyond the primary CREATE TABLE targets). Confirmed no existing CI job provisions a fresh database (no services: block anywhere in ci.yml; lint_migration_schema.py is a static linter checking the opposite direction). Designed a new fresh_database_migration CI job (Postgres 15 service container + zig build migrate against an empty DB, judged by exit code only) as a separate job from build, consistent with that job doc-comment boundary and the existing clean_checkout_lua_build precedent for isolating properties the cached/shared-state job cannot test. Confirmed edit-in-place only (all CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING already idempotent, all 9 files already ledger-applied on long-lived DBs) and confirmed the 35 residual test-integration-svc failures are explicitly out of scope.
